chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and from his father Maymun who said:
We went out with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) to the land of Tayba, and with him were Amr ibn Dinar and a group of his companions. We stayed in Tayba for as long as God willed.

Then Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) rode upon a difficult camel. Amr ibn Dinar said to him: 'How difficult is your camel!' He said: 'Do you not know that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Upon the peak of every camel is a satan, so disgrace it and subdue it, and mention the name of God upon it, for it is God Who carries'?
Then he entered Mecca and we entered with him without ihram.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: Ihram — the ritual state of pilgrim consecration (wearing special garments and observing restrictions)
key_terms.ذِرْوَة: Peak or hump — the highest point of a camel's back
key_terms.شَيْطَان: Satan — here representing the camel's obstinate or wild nature
key_terms.طِيبَة: Tayba — a blessed name for Medina, the city of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Baqir say about riding a difficult camel and remembering God's name?
ai.summary: Maymun ibn al-Qaddah narrates accompanying Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (AS) on a journey from Medina to Mecca. When the Imam mounted a difficult camel, he cited a prophetic tradition that a satan perches on every camel's hump and commanded: subdue it, tame it, and invoke God's name over it, for God alone is the true carrier. The hadith closes with the notable detail that they entered Mecca without ihram, likely indicating an informal non-pilgrimage visit or a jurisprudential circumstance recognized by the Imam.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad, 
(It has been narrated) from Ibn Al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and from his father Maymoun who said,

‘We went out with Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> to the land of Tayba and with him<sup>asws</sup> was Amro Bin Dinar, and a group of his<sup>asws</sup> companions. So we stayed at Tayba for as long as Allah<sup>azwj</sup> so Deisred,

and Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> rode upon a difficult camel. So Amro Bin Dinar said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘How difficult is your<sup>asws</sup> camel’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Or do you not know that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Upon the peak of every camel is a Satan<sup>la</sup>, therefore disgrace it and humiliated it, and mention the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> upon it, for rather it is (the Strength of) Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Who Carries’.
Then heasws entered Makkah and we entered with himasws without Ihraam’.
en.sarwar: 9. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad from ibn al-Qaddah from abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and from his father Maymun who has said the following:

“Once we left with abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, to Ard of Taybah (name of a place between Makkah and al-Madinah) and ‘Amr ibn Dinar was with him (the Imam) as well as other ones of his people. We stopped at Taybah as long as Allah willed,

and abu Ja‘far rode a difficult camel. ‘Amr ibn Dinar said, ‘Your camel is very difficult.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘You must take notice that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said the following. ‘On the peak of every camel there is a Satan, so you must degrade and make him lowly by mentioning the name of Allah on it because He is Allah who carries loads.’
He (the Imam) then entered Makkah and we also entered Makkah without assuming the state of Ihram (because of entering before the passing of a month from his previous Ihram).”’
